_comment: Independent fitness table for build_dispatch_plan()'s _select_workflow(),
authored per Proposal 03 of the orchestration review.
PURPOSE: selection_golden_corpus.json pins build_dispatch_plan()'s current
output as its own regression baseline -- it is derived FROM the code and
therefore cannot catch the code mislabeling something, because a bug in
_select_workflow() and a fixture copied from that same buggy output will
always agree. This file is deliberately NOT derived from _select_workflow()
or from the golden corpus. Every 'expected_workflow' value below was
reasoned independently from roster/workflows/*.md (the human-authored
description of what each workflow shape means) and from routing.json's
route/risk semantics, then checked against selection.schema.json's closed
'workflow' enum. Where an entry's task/changed_files were reused from
selection_golden_corpus.json or test_selector.py (to guarantee a known
route/risk match without re-deriving routing.json's matching rules), the
'reasoning' field says so explicitly -- reuse of INPUT text is fine;
copying the EXPECTED OUTPUT would defeat the point of this file.
test_workflow_fitness_table.py runs build_dispatch_plan() against every
case here and asserts actual workflow == expected_workflow. No case is
currently marked known_mismatch -- see the closing note below for the two
that once were and why they were fixed in the code instead. Deliberate
disagreement with the code under test is the signal this table exists to
produce, so add the flag rather than bending a case to match behavior.
Coverage: at least one case per selection.schema.json workflow enum value
(new-service, product-intake, runtime-assurance, debugging,
infrastructure-change, pipeline-change, knowledge-ingestion,
support-escalation, production-release, rollback, unclassified,
needs-triage).
Scope boundary: this file does not add a new workflow enum value, does
not modify _select_workflow(), and does not add a roster/workflows/*.md
doc. If a case below implies the closed enum is genuinely missing a
shape, that is Proposal 08's territory, not this file's -- see the PR
description for which cases (if any) that applies to.

No case is currently marked known_mismatch. Both that once were have been fixed in the code (#154, #157) rather than weakened here; add the flag for a future disagreement rather than bending a case to match current behavior.
Five cases were added with #210, which replaced _select_workflow()'s
hardcoded four-route-id delivery-shape test with an explicit per-route
'workflow_shape' in routing.json. They cover what that change made
expressible and what it must not swallow: a narrow execution route
contributing new-service on its own; execution routes contributing
infrastructure-change and pipeline-change rather than the new-service
their primary role's 'build' catalog phase would have implied; and two
execution routes that must stay unclassified (verify-phase test
authoring, security-phase control work), which is the failure mode the
issue's rejected naive fix would have produced.
Six 'WF-SHAPE-PIN-*' cases exist for a different reason than the rest of
this file. They are not here because their workflow was in doubt -- all
six are ordinary new-service delivery work -- but because
test_workflow_shape_coverage.py found their routes' workflow_shape
declarations pinned by nothing: every other fixture matching them also
matched a broad route already contributing new-service, so the
declaration could be edited to any legal value with a green suite. Each
one's input is constructed to match its route WITHOUT a broad route
co-matching, which is what makes the declaration decisive. Their
'reasoning' records both the shape judgment and the isolation technique,
since the latter is fragile: it depends on which keywords the broad
route currently claims. If one of these stops isolating, the coverage
test fails and names the route rather than the fixture silently
measuring nothing.

cases.description: backend-only build route -> new-service
cases.task: Implement a backend API for user upload
cases.reasoning: new-service.md: 'covers work that proceeds beyond intake into design and delivery.' A backend route match (one of the build-shaped routes: frontend/backend/infrastructure/pipeline) implementing a new API endpoint is squarely design-and-delivery work, not a narrower recognized shape (not infra/pipeline-only, not a defect fix, not intake-only). Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's BACKEND-1 to guarantee the route match; the expected workflow value was derived independently from new-service.md, not copied from BACKEND-1's (unasserted) workflow.

cases.description: architecture-change risk with no build-shaped route -> new-service
cases.task: Design the architecture and system design proposal
cases.reasoning: new-service.md step 3 names the architecture phase (Cloud Architect, G3) as an explicit stage of this same lifecycle shape, so a task that trips routing.json's 'architecture-change' risk rule (System Architect boundary/ADR work) belongs to new-service even when no frontend/backend/infrastructure/pipeline route also matched. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's ARCHITECTURE-DESIGN-1.

cases.description: product-intent route only -> product-intake
cases.task: Capture the product intent for the new mission objective
cases.reasoning: product-intake.md: 'Use this workflow when work has not yet entered architecture or implementation.' Drafting the versioned intent record is literally step 2 of product-intake.md, before any G2/architecture handoff. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's PRODUCT-INTENT-1.

cases.description: requirements-baseline route only -> product-intake
cases.task: Perform requirements decomposition and requirements traceability
cases.reasoning: product-intake.md step 4: Requirements Agent decomposes approved intent into requirement IDs/acceptance criteria/traceability -- the requirements-baseline route's own G1/G2 quality_gates in routing.json match product-intake.md's G1/G2 handoff, still strictly before new-service.md's G3 architecture stage. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's REQUIREMENTS-BASELINE-1.

cases.description: runtime-assurance route only -> runtime-assurance
cases.task: Observe production runtime conformance for deployed behavior
cases.reasoning: runtime-assurance.md's own flowchart (Observability SRE observes -> Security/Compliance review -> G10 Service Owner decides) is precisely this task's shape. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's RUNTIME-ASSURANCE-1.

cases.description: backend+testing+debugging routes, explicit defect investigation -> debugging
cases.task: Debug a panic and identify the root cause from the stack trace
cases.reasoning: debugging.md step 2: 'Reproduce the issue or prove it is unreproducible, isolate the smallest likely cause.' This task is a textbook reproduce/root-cause/fix case -- an actual defect, not routine maintenance (contrast with WF-AGENT-SUITE-GOVERNANCE-MISLABEL-1 below). Task/file reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's DEBUGGING-1.

cases.description: infrastructure route only -> infrastructure-change
cases.task: Update Terraform for a Proxmox worker VM
cases.reasoning: infrastructure-change.md's Classify -> Provision+Plan -> Infrastructure Reviewer -> gated approval -> Apply shape is exactly an IaC-only change with no frontend/backend/pipeline overlap. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's INFRA-1.
cases.known_gate: infrastructure-change.md cross-checks G3/G4/G5/G6/G7/G8 against routing.json's infrastructure route -- consistent with no risk rule firing here.

cases.description: pipeline route only -> pipeline-change
cases.task: Change the GitLab pipeline runner configuration
cases.reasoning: pipeline-change.md's Document -> Test -> Pipeline Security Reviewer -> gated approval -> Enable shape covers exactly a CI/CD runner-configuration change. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's PIPELINE-1.

cases.description: knowledge-store route only -> knowledge-ingestion
cases.task: Tune the knowledge store retrieval and embedding vector search
cases.reasoning: knowledge-ingestion.md's Record -> Security/Compliance review -> Normalize -> Redact -> Ingest -> Evaluate -> Evidence shape is the recognized shape for knowledge-store-only work; nothing else (no frontend/backend/infra/pipeline/debugging) also matched. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's KNOWLEDGE-STORE-1.

cases.description: support route only -> support-escalation
cases.task: Provide user report triage and a workaround for a customer issue
cases.reasoning: support-escalation.md's Triage -> Investigate -> Escalate -> Closure shape is exactly a customer-ticket triage/workaround task. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's SUPPORT-1.

cases.description: incident-response route, task mentions 'rollback' but the action described is coordination/escalation, not execution -> support-escalation, NOT rollback
cases.task: Coordinate rollback during a sev1 major incident postmortem
cases.reasoning: Deliberately placed next to WF-ROLLBACK-GAP-1 below to show the two are genuinely different shapes, not the same shape mislabeled two different ways. This task's verb is 'coordinate' during a sev1/postmortem/war-room incident -- that is support-escalation.md's Triage/Investigate/Escalate/'Human escalation' shape (an accountable human decides on the production action while the incident is being managed). rollback.md instead describes the release engineer's concrete execution playbook ('Release engineer selects the pre-approved rollback... obtain emergency authorization... deploy known-good artifact') once a decision has already been made. Incident coordination is not artifact-rollback execution, so support-escalation is the correct label for this specific task text even though it contains the word 'rollback'. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's INCIDENT-RESPONSE-1.

cases.description: infrastructure route + production risk -> production-release
cases.task: Deploy to production with Terraform
cases.reasoning: production-release.md's G8 precondition-check -> G9 deploy-immutable-artifact -> verify -> G10 shape matches routing.json's 'production' risk rule (deploy/release/production keyword groups) exactly. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's PRODUCTION-RISK-1.

cases.description: an explicit rollback-execution task; fixed in #157 by a rollback route plus a branch ahead of the production risk check
cases.task: Roll back the production release to the last known-good artifact after failed verification
cases.reasoning: rollback.md's Trigger -> Preserve Evidence -> Release Engineer selects known-good procedure -> emergency human authorization -> Deploy known-good artifact -> Verify shape is exactly this task. Before #157 'rollback' was an enumerated, documented workflow no plan could be assigned: the production risk check ran first and swallowed it. The branch now runs ahead of that check, and excludes incident-coordination framing so a task merely mentioning rollback stays support-escalation.

cases.description: governance-planning route only, no recognized shape -> unclassified
cases.task: Assess governance impact and data jurisdiction
cases.reasoning: unclassified.md: emitted when 'the selector matched at least one route or risk rule... but the matched combination does not fit any of this repository's recognized workflow shapes.' governance-planning is a narrow advisory/review route with its own AGENT.md but no dedicated roster/workflows/*.md shape (it contributes to new-service.md step 2 as one participant among several, but is never itself a whole recognized shape). Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's GOVERNANCE-PLANNING-1.

cases.description: no route/risk match -> needs-triage
cases.task: Investigate an unexplained issue
cases.reasoning: AGENTS.md/RUNBOOK.md: 'If no rule matches a task, the selector returns needs-triage rather than guessing.' Trivial by construction: no selected agents means _select_workflow()'s first check (`if not has_agents: return "needs-triage"`) is the only defensible answer. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's NEEDS-TRIAGE-1.

cases.description: routine roster/catalog maintenance with no defect present -- the review's named case, fixed by PR #154's agent-suite-maintenance workflow
cases.task: add a new specialist role to the roster
cases.reasoning: agent-suite-maintenance.md covers maintenance of this repository's own role catalog, routing rules, and orchestration tooling -- work where the roster machinery is the subject, not the tool. Adding a role is exactly that. Before #154 this returned 'debugging', because _select_workflow() mapped every agent-suite-governance match there unconditionally; that branch now distinguishes a keyword-driven debugging hit from a path-only roster edit, so a routine catalog change no longer reads as defect investigation.

cases.description: two build-shaped routes (frontend+backend) -> new-service
cases.task: Add a React upload form backed by a PostgreSQL API
cases.reasoning: Same reasoning as WF-NEW-SERVICE-1, extended to confirm a multi-route build case (frontend+backend) still resolves to the single new-service shape rather than being treated as ambiguous. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's CROSS-STACK-1.

cases.description: a single narrow execution route, no broad route co-matching -> new-service
cases.task: Implement Node TypeScript utility
cases.reasoning: new-service.md: 'covers work that proceeds beyond intake into design and delivery. Use product-intake.md when the task only captures intent or baselines requirements.' Writing a Node/TypeScript build utility is delivery of application code -- it is past intake, it is not a defect fix, it provisions no infrastructure, and it defines no pipeline -- so of the twelve documented shapes only new-service describes it. Derived from new-service.md and the node-typescript-implementer role's own scope, not from _select_workflow(): this case is here specifically because the same input returned 'unclassified' before #210, when only four hardcoded route ids could contribute a shape. Task/files reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's NODE-TYPESCRIPT-EXECUTION-1 to guarantee the route match.

cases.description: a single narrow infrastructure-shaped execution route -> infrastructure-change
cases.task: Implement ansible automation implementation
cases.reasoning: infrastructure-change.md's shape is Classify -> Provision+Plan -> Infrastructure Reviewer -> gated approval -> Apply. Ansible playbooks, roles, and inventories are declarative host configuration applied to real machines, and the ansible-automation-implementer role is accountable to infrastructure-provisioner with an independent infrastructure review -- that is the same review and apply shape, not application delivery. Distinguishes the declared shape from the primary role's catalog phase, which is 'build' here: a phase-derived rule would have called this new-service. Task reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's ANSIBLE_AUTOMATION_EXECUTION_GOLDEN_1 to guarantee the route match in isolation.

cases.description: a single narrow delivery-automation execution route -> pipeline-change
cases.task: Implement gitops delivery implementation
cases.reasoning: pipeline-change.md's step 1 names the artifacts it governs: 'the execution graph, trust boundaries, runner types, triggers, permissions, secret exposure, artifact flow, environments, and rollback behavior.' Argo CD/Flux applications and sync waves are exactly artifact flow, environments, and rollback behavior; the gitops-delivery-implementer role's own escalation list ('promotion, environment approval, production sync, rollback') is that same vocabulary. It configures how releases reach an environment, not what the platform is made of, so pipeline-change rather than infrastructure-change. Task reused verbatim from selection_golden_corpus.json's GITOPS_DELIVERY_EXECUTION_GOLDEN_1.

cases.description: a verify-phase execution route claims no delivery shape -> unclassified
cases.task: Implement typescript test implementation
cases.reasoning: unclassified.md: emitted when the selector 'matched at least one route or risk rule... but the matched combination does not fit any of this repository's recognized workflow shapes,' and 'unclassified means a statement about workflow-shape recognition, not about the task's actual impact.' Authoring TypeScript tests is real delivery work, but none of the twelve roster/workflows/*.md shapes is test authoring: new-service.md places Verification inside a full G1-G10 intent-to-runtime lifecycle, which a standalone test-writing task is not, and runtime-assurance.md is about observing deployed behavior. This case exists to hold the line against the naive fix the issue rejected (any '*-execution' route implies new-service, measured at 68 golden failures); it is the one of #210's three named fixtures whose 'unclassified' was correct all along, and it is correct now for a stated reason rather than because no route could contribute a shape. If a test-authoring workflow doc is ever added, this is the case to revisit.

cases.description: a security-phase execution route claims no delivery shape -> unclassified
cases.task: Implement secure boot implementation
cases.reasoning: Secure-boot work is governed by the security review and G5 authority that new-service.md lists as one stage among ten, not by the intent-to-runtime lifecycle as a whole, and no roster/workflows/*.md describes a security-control change end to end. unclassified.md's step 3 is the correct disposition for that: proceed on the plan's own required_quality_gates and human_gates, and propose a new shape if the combination recurs. Recorded so a later broadening of new-service to 'anything a build-capable role implements' has to argue with this case rather than pass silently.

cases.description: python-automation-execution in isolation -> new-service (pins its declared shape)
cases.task: Maintain the automation script
cases.reasoning: new-service.md covers 'work that proceeds beyond intake into design and delivery'. A Python automation script under scripts/ is a delivered code artifact: it is not infrastructure (it provisions no host, cluster, or network), not a pipeline definition (it is not a CI/CD execution graph), and not intake-only. Its input is constructed rather than reused, specifically so this route matches without a broad route (frontend/backend/ai-feature) co-matching -- otherwise the broad route already contributes new-service and this route's own declaration is decorative, which is what test_workflow_shape_coverage.py measures. `scripts/**` is in the frontend route's exclude_paths and matches no backend path glob, and the task text avoids backend's 'python' keyword, so the executor route stands alone.

cases.description: go-service-execution in isolation -> new-service (pins its declared shape)
cases.task: Implement the go implementation for the exporter
cases.reasoning: Implementing a Go service is the archetypal new-service.md case -- design-and-delivery of service code, the same reasoning as WF-NEW-SERVICE-1's backend API. Its input is constructed rather than reused, specifically so this route matches without a broad route (frontend/backend/ai-feature) co-matching -- otherwise the broad route already contributes new-service and this route's own declaration is decorative, which is what test_workflow_shape_coverage.py measures. Matching by keyword with no changed files is what isolates it: any *.go path would also match the backend route, and the word 'golang' would match backend's keyword list, so the task says 'go implementation' and carries no files.

cases.description: react-component-execution in isolation -> new-service (pins its declared shape)
cases.task: Implement jsx component
cases.reasoning: A React/JSX component is frontend application code, and the frontend route already resolves to new-service for exactly this kind of change (selection_golden_corpus.json's FRONTEND-1), so the narrow executor must agree rather than contradict it. Its input is constructed rather than reused, specifically so this route matches without a broad route (frontend/backend/ai-feature) co-matching -- otherwise the broad route already contributes new-service and this route's own declaration is decorative, which is what test_workflow_shape_coverage.py measures. The word 'jsx' avoids frontend's bare 'react' keyword, and frontend's keyword_groups need a typescript/javascript term alongside a UI term, so neither fires.

cases.description: postgres-query-execution without the backend route -> new-service (pins its declared shape)
cases.task: Refine the stored query definitions
cases.reasoning: Query implementation is backend delivery work: it produces code the service executes, not infrastructure and not a pipeline. Its input is constructed rather than reused, specifically so this route matches without a broad route (frontend/backend/ai-feature) co-matching -- otherwise the broad route already contributes new-service and this route's own declaration is decorative, which is what test_workflow_shape_coverage.py measures. Isolating this one is unusually narrow: every keyword the route declares ('postgres query', 'postgresql query', 'pgx query') contains a backend keyword, and any *.sql file matches backend's path globs, so the input is a non-SQL generator config under postgres/queries/ with a task naming neither product nor engine. The co-matched database-reliability route declares unclassified and contributes nothing, which is what leaves this route's declaration decisive.

cases.description: frontend-accessibility-remediation-execution without the frontend route -> new-service (pins its declared shape)
cases.task: Apply the a11y remediation
cases.reasoning: Accessibility remediation edits frontend application code, which new-service.md's Implementation stage covers and which FRONTEND-1 already labels new-service for the same subject matter (keyboard accessibility). Its input is constructed rather than reused, specifically so this route matches without a broad route (frontend/backend/ai-feature) co-matching -- otherwise the broad route already contributes new-service and this route's own declaration is decorative, which is what test_workflow_shape_coverage.py measures. Both of the route's path globs sit under frontend/**, and two of its three keywords contain frontend's bare 'accessibility' keyword, so the only isolating input is the 'a11y remediation' phrasing with no changed files -- 'a11y' appears solely in frontend's second keyword_group, which cannot fire without a typescript/javascript term from the first.

cases.description: inference-gateway-execution without the ai-feature route -> new-service (pins its declared shape)
cases.task: Update the gateway timeout configuration
cases.reasoning: Model API adapters, timeouts, retries, and budgets are delivered service code -- the gateway is a service the product calls, so new-service.md's design-and-delivery shape applies, not infrastructure-change (it configures no platform) and not pipeline-change (it defines no delivery flow). Its input is constructed rather than reused, specifically so this route matches without a broad route (frontend/backend/ai-feature) co-matching -- otherwise the broad route already contributes new-service and this route's own declaration is decorative, which is what test_workflow_shape_coverage.py measures. The route's own keyword contains 'inference', an ai-feature keyword, so the isolating input matches by path instead, using a non-.go config file (a *.go path would pull in both backend and go-service-execution).
